outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Enterprise software & cybersecurity, led by CrowdStrike, Salesforce, ServiceNow and Zscaler
strongest.reason: these names rallied sharply in premarket trading even as the broader AI-infrastructure complex sold off, reinforcing the view that they're viewed as beneficiaries of AI adoption rather than casualties of a slower frontier-model buildout

strongest.area: Crypto, led by Bitcoin and Ethereum
strongest.reason: both climbed while Nasdaq futures fell sharply on the AI-pacing news, a notable decoupling from the broader tech selloff, helped by rising odds of the CLARITY Act passing this year

weakest.area: Memory & AI compute chips, led by Micron, AMD, ASML and Teradyne
weakest.reason: these names were among the hardest-hit in premarket trading after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's essay calling for AI developers to slow the pace of frontier model development, which triggered a broad reassessment of AI infrastructure spending

weakest.area: AI infrastructure bellwethers, including Nvidia, Broadcom, Oracle and TSMC
weakest.reason: even the largest, most established names in the AI buildout fell 2-4% in premarket trading, suggesting the selloff is hitting the AI-compute theme broadly rather than being confined to smaller or more speculative names

outlook.nextStep: The dominant story is Dario Amodei's 'We Must Pace the Frontier' essay, echoed by Sam Altman and Elon Musk over the weekend, which triggered a broad premarket selloff across chips and AI infrastructure — worth close attention this week for whether any hyperscaler actually signals a capex pullback, since that's what would validate this repricing rather than reverse it once the regular session opens. The Sept 15-16 FOMC decision layers a second major catalyst on top, with the 10-year yield still hovering near 5%. The sharp divergence between falling chip/hardware names and rallying enterprise software and crypto is probably better watched for a few sessions than acted on immediately, since premarket moves can overstate or reverse once full-session volume comes in.

signals.title: Anthropic CEO's 'pace the frontier' essay triggers broad AI-chip selloff
signals.body: Dario Amodei published a roughly 3,800-word essay over the weekend urging AI developers to slow the pace of frontier model capability gains, citing safety concerns. Nasdaq 100 futures fell over 1% Sunday night, and AI-linked chip and infrastructure names dropped sharply in Monday's premarket session, with memory and equipment names among the hardest hit. Sam Altman and Elon Musk both publicly echoed the sentiment.
signals.watch: NVDA, AMD, MU, ASML, AVGO, TSM
signals.focus: the single biggest overnight catalyst across the whole tracker; worth close attention for whether it's a one-session repricing or the start of a more sustained reassessment of AI capex

signals.title: Fed decision Sept 15-16 looms with 10-year yield near 5%
signals.body: The 10-year Treasury yield held just under 5% — its highest area since October 2023 — heading into Tuesday and Wednesday's FOMC meeting, with markets still pricing meaningful odds of a rate move.
signals.focus: the second major catalyst of the week; probably better watched than traded ahead of Wednesday's decision

signals.title: Oil extends its climb on new Saudi pipeline attack
signals.body: WTI pushed further above $100 a barrel after fresh attacks over the weekend targeted a Saudi Arabian oil pipeline, homes and a mosque, adding a second geopolitical risk premium on top of the ongoing Strait of Hormuz tensions.
signals.focus: worth monitoring for follow-through, especially given the added inflation-pressure angle heading into the Fed meeting

signals.title: Memory and storage names hit hardest in the AI-pacing selloff
signals.body: Micron led memory-chip names lower in premarket trading as investors reassessed AI infrastructure spending assumptions following the Amodei essay, with the broader storage and memory complex among the session's biggest decliners.
signals.focus: the sharpest single-day move in the tracker; worth watching closely for whether it extends into the regular session or partially reverses

signals.title: Enterprise software and cybersecurity rally as capital rotates out of AI infrastructure
signals.body: CrowdStrike, Salesforce, ServiceNow and Zscaler all jumped in premarket trading, a sharp divergence from the falling chip and AI-infrastructure complex, consistent with the ongoing narrative that AI is more a tailwind than a threat for SaaS and security platforms.
signals.focus: a continuing trend worth tracking, though the scale of today's rotation is unusually large and may partly unwind once full-session trading begins

signals.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum decouple from the AI-driven tech selloff
signals.body: Bitcoin climbed toward $78,000 and Ethereum gained roughly 2% even as Nasdaq 100 futures fell over 1% on the AI-pacing news — an unusual divergence that some are attributing to crypto being viewed as insulated from AI-capex-specific concerns, plus rising odds of the CLARITY Act passing this year.
signals.focus: worth watching to see whether this decoupling holds through the week or crypto eventually follows equities lower

signals.title: Oracle's Ellison cancels planned $7.5B stock sale
signals.body: Oracle Executive Chairman Larry Ellison canceled his 10b5-1 plan to sell up to 50 million shares (roughly $7.5B) over the weekend, with the company saying no stock was sold under the plan. Oracle shares nonetheless fell in Monday's premarket session, swept up in the broader AI-linked selloff.
signals.focus: a notable insider-confidence signal worth noting, though it wasn't enough to offset the broader AI-pacing selloff today
